lyrics:
[Intro: synth pad, soft drum tick, bass pulse, sustained guitar note]

[Verse 1: low murmur over bass and tick]
I see the keys in your hand
I see the coat that you won't put down
You're a tide that can't decide
And I'm the shore, I don't make a sound

[Verse 2: kick drum enters]
I've been the cure and the thirst
I've been the lock and I've been the thief
You hand me just enough of you
To keep me, to keep me on my knees

[Chorus: still restrained, quiet]
Halfway out the door
Halfway in my arms
I can't hold you here
I can't let you go far
Halfway out the door

[Verse 3: voice rises an octave, floor tom joins]
Maybe it's you, maybe a town
Maybe a God that I can't put down
Something I love is taking me slow
And I'd fall, I'd fall if it let me go

[Chorus: shimmering delay guitar enters, snare begins]
Halfway out the door
Halfway in my arms
I can't hold you here
I can't let you go far
Halfway out the door

[Build: wordless rising vocal, every instrument growing]
Oh, oh, oh, oh
(Stay) Oh, oh, oh, oh
(Go) Oh, oh, oh, oh
(Stay) Oh, oh, oh, oh

[Chorus: climax, full drums, crashing cymbals, full-voice cry]
Halfway out the door!
Halfway in my arms!
I can't hold you here
I can't let you go far
Halfway out the door

[Instrumental: chiming delay guitar, descending, calming]

[Outro: bass and one guitar note, whispered, unresolved]
I see the keys in your hand
I see the keys in my own
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 108 BPM, 4/4, C major, on one four-chord loop (I-V-vi-IV) that never changes from first bar to last. A slow burn: it starts as a whisper and takes three minutes to catch fire.

VOICE: Male voice that begins as a low, breathy murmur, almost spoken, barely above the bass. Each section sits a little higher and fuller, until the build section breaks into a full-throated, open-vowel wordless cry at the top of his range. The coda returns to a fragile near-whisper. Faint backing voices whisper 'stay' and 'go' under the cry.

INSTRUMENTS: A bass guitar playing steady, pulsing eighth notes on the root of each chord (the spine). A soft drum-machine tick that is later joined, then replaced, by a live kit with a booming floor tom and a late-arriving snare. A sustained, endless, violin-like electric guitar note that hovers over everything (the earworm atmosphere). Shimmering, rhythmically delayed guitar arpeggios that only enter in the second half. A warm, barely-there synth pad.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, synth pad and drum tick, then the bass pulse and the endless sustained guitar note. 0:27 Verse 1, murmured voice over bass and tick. 0:53 Verse 2, kick drum enters. 1:20 Chorus 1, still restrained, a higher harmony guitar note appears. 1:42 Verse 3, the voice rises an octave, floor tom joins. 2:09 Chorus 2, the delayed arpeggio guitar finally enters and the snare begins. 2:31 Build, wordless 'oh' rising across 8 bars as every instrument grows. 2:58 Climax chorus, full kit, crashing cymbals, voice at full cry. 3:20 Instrumental, the delayed guitar plays a simple, chiming, descending figure as the storm recedes. 3:47 Coda, back to bass and one guitar note, the final two lines nearly whispered, ending unresolved at 4:15.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Spacious, atmospheric and patient. Huge natural reverbs and long delays, the bass warm and dominant early, the dynamic range left wide so the climax is truly louder.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The wordless cry at 2:31-2:58. After two and a half minutes of holding back, the voice lets go.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: A deep sub under the bass pulse and a wider, more immersive reverb field. The whispered 'stay / go' backing voices are a new layer, panned to opposite sides.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Restraint, ache, eruption, then exhausted tenderness.

WHAT IT IS ABOUT

Someone stands in a doorway with keys in hand and a coat they won't put down. The singer can't hold them and can't release them. In the last line, the keys turn out to be in the singer's own hand too.

THE OTHER WAYS TO HEAR IT

Hear it as: a relationship stuck between leaving and staying; faith that won't go and won't settle ('a God that I can't put down'); a hometown you love and need to escape; a habit you can't quit; or an adult child and an ageing parent. The final line reverses the whole song: maybe the narrator is the one who is halfway out.

ENGINEERED HOOKS AND THE DESIGNED MISHEARING

Borrowed mechanics: a single paradox as the entire lyric, an unidentified 'you', four chords that never change, and a climax where words are replaced by a wordless cry. The backing voices whisper 'stay' and 'go' under the cry so the listener hears whichever they need. Designed mishearing: 'Halfway out the door' is heard as 'Half the way I adore'.
